## Review

::: {.takeaway}
Test MSE is the quantity we want. One train and test split estimates it noisily,
and costs us data.
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.question}
You split `Auto` in half on Friday. What happens with a different split?
:::
:::

## Limitations {.small}

::: {.incremental}
1. The estimate depends heavily on which split was drawn  
2. Fitting on a subset overstates the error of the deployed model  
:::

# LOOCV {.center}

## LOOCV

![](img/islp/fig5_3.png){fig-align="center" width="76%"}

::: {.source}
ISLP Figure 5.3. Each observation takes a turn as a validation set of size one.
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$\text{CV}_{(n)} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\text{MSE}_i$$
:::

## k-fold cross-validation

![](img/islp/fig5_5.png){fig-align="center" width="78%"}

::: {.source}
ISLP Figure 5.5. Five fold cross-validation. Each fifth takes a turn as the
validation set.
:::

::: {.fragment}
$$\text{CV}_{(k)} = \frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=1}^{k}\text{MSE}_j$$
:::

## LOOCV and 10-fold CV

![](img/islp/fig5_4.png){fig-align="center" width="84%"}

::: {.source}
ISLP Figure 5.4. Left: the LOOCV error curve on `Auto`. Right: 10-fold CV run
nine times with different random splits.
:::

## CV against true test MSE

![](img/islp/fig5_6.png){fig-align="center" width="86%"}

::: {.source}
ISLP Figure 5.6. True test MSE in blue, LOOCV as a black dashed line, and
10-fold CV in orange, for the data of Figures 2.9 to 2.11.
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.takeaway}
CV can miss the level. It finds the location of the minimum.
:::
:::

## Choosing k {.small}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### LOOCV

Low bias, since each fit uses $n-1$ points.

High variance, since the $n$ fits are nearly identical and their errors are
correlated.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### $k = 5$ or $k = 10$

A little bias.

Lower variance.

$k$ fits rather than $n$.
:::

::::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.takeaway}
Bias and variance, applied to the estimator itself.
:::
:::

# In Python {.center}

## cross_val_score {.small}

::: {#b2030e10 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
DATA = "https://lucymcgowan.github.io/sta-363-f26/data/"
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score, KFold
from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import make_pipeline

Auto = pd.read_csv(DATA + "Auto.csv")
X = Auto[["horsepower"]]
y = Auto["mpg"]

model = make_pipeline(PolynomialFeatures(2), LinearRegression())
cv = KFold(n_splits=10, shuffle=True, random_state=363)
scores = -cross_val_score(model, X, y, cv=cv, scoring="neg_mean_squared_error")
scores.round(2)
```
